$comment: Operational knobs. Anything the spec called a placeholder is marked PLACEHOLDER and needs a real value from Alex before go-live.

llm.$comment: Temperature 0 on classifier and extractor per the spec's drift note. Draft generation is the one place a hair of variation is fine, but it runs at 0 too so the three-pass fixture check stays honest.

staleFollowUp.$comment_thresholdDays: PLACEHOLDER. Spec STL-01/02 assume 5. Confirm the real number with Alex.
staleFollowUp.$comment_businessDaysOnly: OPEN QUESTION. Left off so STL-01 counts days the way the spec writes them (day 0 to day 6 is 6). Turn it on and a Friday send would not surface until the following Friday, which is probably what a person actually wants. Alex decides.
staleFollowUp.$comment_threadAware: STL-03: any inbound on the same conversation counts as an answer, no matter who sent it.

learning.$comment_singleActionCap: LRN-03 overfitting guard. Any sender sitting on a tier with a weight floor gets its per-action movement clamped to this, and can never be pushed below the floor. One delete cannot knock a key client down.

dailySummary.$comment_criticalDeadlineHorizonDays: SUMX-02 sets the floor on this. CLS-01 arrives 2026-01-15 with a 2026-02-14 bid date, 30 days out, and the spec requires that date under Critical Deadlines the same day. So the horizon has to clear a normal bid cycle. It exists only to keep an absurd far-future date out of the brief.

integration.$comment_approvalGate: INT-03 red line. 'required' means every outbound write to Pipedrive, SharePoint or the R: drive is queued as a pending intent and logged as a dry run. Nothing hits a live system until a human clears it. Do not set this to 'off'.

drafts.$comment_neverCreateFor: Bid Outcome is off the auto-draft list on purpose. An award or a loss is a message Alex answers himself.
